decisions.reason: Selecting new LED power-switching transistors does not change the existing component sourceability or cost policies.
The BOM transistor update does not change the requirement to assist with manufacturer settings, pricing, availability review, or ordering.
Updating transistor selections in the documentation does not alter the requirement for portable KiCad project resources.
The candidate already contains a complete same-message MODIFY recording the N-channel/P-channel topology and the IRLML2402 and IRLML6402 transistor selections.
The new transistors concern LED power switching, not the established 3.3V LED supply or direct ESP32 data-drive logic; the historical IRLML2402 level-shifter detail was already removed.
The new transistors are for the separately controlled LED power switch and do not change the independent GPIO-switched 5V sensor rail.
The transistor update does not change the LED board's count, LED model, package, part number, or color format.
Changing LED power-switching transistors does not alter the monitored rails, monitoring IC, channel allocation, or measurement coverage.
The IRLML2402 reference appears only in historical discussion of LED circuitry and does not affect the standalone USB regulator requirement or its unresolved current-capacity question.
The LED switching-transistor update does not modify the AXP2101 battery, USB, VMID, VSYS, or DCDC1 power path.
The transistor update is unrelated to battery connector placement, orientation, spacing, or mounting-hole clearance.
The new LED power-switching transistors do not alter the DCDC1 configured voltage, target rail voltage, or Schottky-drop compensation requirement.
